previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for post-procedural observation after undergoing transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) of a 5.2 cm liver tumor in segment VI/VII and smaller lesions in segment VIII. The procedure was uncomplicated, with successful delivery of doxorubicin-lipiodol and no non-target embolization. He remained stable throughout admission, with no significant pain, nausea, or complications. Post-procedure CT confirmed good lipiodol uptake in the target lesions and no ectopic distribution. Liver enzymes rose modestly as expected. He was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor for post-embolization symptoms, complete outpatient lab testing, and follow up with oncology and hepatology. All home medications, including nadolol, diuretics, and omeprazole, were continued.

TACE procedure report preliminary:
HISTORY: ___ needed TACE procedure.
 
COMPARISON: MR of the abdomen from ___.
 
TECHNIQUE: OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiology 
fellow) and Dr.

procedure. The
attending was present and supervising throughout the procedure.
 
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating 
divided doses of
100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed throughout the total 
intra-service time
of 2 hours and 50 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic 
parameters
were continuously monitored.
 
MEDICATIONS: 40 mg of intra-arterial doxirubicin eluting beads 
(100-300
micron), 100 mcg of intra-arterial nitroglycerin, 30 mg of 
intra-venous
toradol.
 
CONTRAST: 135 ml of Optiray.
 
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 55.4 min, 1712 mGy
 
PROCEDURE:
 
1. Right common femoral artery access.
2. Celiac arteriogram.
3. Common hepatic arteriogram with cone beam CT.
4. Right hepatic arteriogram x 2.
5. Embolization of two branches of the right hepatic artery with 
40 mg of
doxirubicin eluted on 100-300 micron beads.
6. Attempted catheterization of a right phrenic artery.
 
PROCEDURE DETAILS:
 
Following a discussion of the risks, benefits and alternatives 
to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained. The patient 
was placed
supine on the imaging table and both groins were prepped and 
draped in the
usual sterile fashion and a pre-procedure time out was performed 
using 3
patient identifiers.
 
Using palpatory and fluoroscopic guidance, the right common 
femoral artery was
punctured using a micropuncture set. A small skin incision was 
made over the
needle. Then the inner dilator and nitinol wire were removed and 
___
wire was advanced under fluoroscopy into the aorta. The 
micropuncture sheath
was exchanged for a 5 ___ sheath which was attached to a 
heparinized saline
side arm flush.
 
A C2 Cobra catheter was advanced over ___ wire into the 
aorta. The wire
was removed and the celiac artery was selectively cannulated and 
a small
contrast injection was made to confirm position. A common 
hepatic arteriogram
was performed. A Renegade ___ microcatheter pre-loaded with a 
double angled
Glidewire was used to access two separate branches of the right 
hepatic artery
and arteriograms were performed from each branch. Embolization 
was performed
of both branches of the right hepatic artery with 40 mg of 
doxirubicin eluted
on to 100-300 micron beads.
 
The C2 Cobra catheters and ___ wire was used to access the 
left external
iliac artery and the C2 was exchanged for a ___ catheter 
over the wire.
The ___ catheter and a Renegade microcatheter pre-loaded 
with a double
angled Glidewire were used to attempt access to an inferior 
phrenic artery.
After multiple attempts, the procedure was ended given the 
amount of contrast
and radiation used.
 
The catheters and wire were then drawn. The sheath was removed 
and manual
pressure was held for 15 min. Sterile dressings were applied. 
The patient
tolerated the procedure well.
 
FINDINGS:
 
1. Conventional hepatic arterial anatomy with two branches 
supplying tumor in
segment VI and VII. The cystic artery is noted to arise from the 
right
hepatic artery but likely a separate branch than the ones from 
which tumor is
supplied.
2. Pre-embolization arteriogram showing tumor blush in segment 
___.
3. Post-embolization showing staining of tumors in VI and VII.
4. Unsuccessful attempts at catheterization of a right phrenic 
artery, which
may be supplying the medial portion of the large segment VII 
tumor.
 
IMPRESSION:
Successful right common femoral artery approach trans-arterial
chemoembolization of segment VI and VII hepatocellular 
carcinoma.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ needed TACE procedure.

COMPARISON:  MR of the abdomen from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ radiology fellow) and Dr.
___ radiology attending) performed the procedure.  The
attending was present and supervising throughout the procedure.  

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed throughout the total intra-service time

were continuously monitored.

micron), 100 mcg of intra-arterial nitroglycerin, 30 mg of intra-venous
toradol.

CONTRAST: 135 ml of Optiray.

1.  Right common femoral artery access.
2.  Celiac arteriogram.
3.  Common hepatic arteriogram with cone beam CT.
4.  Right hepatic arteriogram x 2.
5.  Embolization of two branches of the right hepatic artery with 40 mg of

6.  Attempted catheterization of a right phrenic artery.

procedure, written informed consent was obtained. The patient was placed
supine on the imaging table and both groins were prepped and draped in the
usual sterile fashion and a pre-procedure time out was performed using 3

Using palpatory and fluoroscopic guidance, the right common femoral artery was
punctured using a micropuncture set.  A small skin incision was made over the
needle.  Then the inner dilator and nitinol wire were removed and ___
wire was advanced under fluoroscopy into the aorta.  The micropuncture sheath
was exchanged for a 5 ___ sheath which was attached to a heparinized saline
side arm flush.

A C2 Cobra catheter was advanced over ___ wire into the aorta. The wire
was removed and the celiac artery was selectively cannulated and a small
contrast injection was made to confirm position.  A common hepatic arteriogram

Glidewire was used to access two separate branches of the right hepatic artery

iliac artery and the C2 was exchanged for a ___ catheter over the wire.
The ___ catheter and a Renegade microcatheter pre-loaded with a double

Rotational cone-beam CT angiography was performed.  Multiplanar CT images were
reconstructed and 3D volume-rendered images of the arterial anatomy required

1.  Conventional hepatic arterial anatomy with two branches supplying tumor in

4.  Unsuccessful attempts at catheterization of a right phrenic artery, which
may be supplying the medial portion of the large segment VII tumor.

Successful right common femoral artery approach trans-arterial
